subject: Live chat slowdown — rapid response and mitigation
messages:
From: Evan Marshall <evan@evergreen-ai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Livechat streaming delays starting ~09:00 PDT

Hi Jonas,

Heads up — around 09:00 PDT our customers started seeing long pauses in the live support chat powered by Redwood streaming. The UI shows the spinner for several seconds then a burst of tokens arrives. Affected conversations are sporadic but frequent enough to be noticed across 3 regions (us-west primarily). We see sequence gaps in websocket frames and a handful of request-ids: r-8a3f, r-8a7c, r-8b01.

Customer impact: intermittent long pauses (~5–12s) between chunks; throughput otherwise nominal. We tracked this to streaming endpoints only — polling /generate remains fast.

Can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side? We can pull more traces if needed. Any immediate mitigations we should apply client-side while you triage?

I attached a short HAR of the websocket frames and one sample request-id trace.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Marshall
Head of Integrations, Evergreen AI
[e: evan@evergreen-ai.com]
[Attachment: chat_trace.har (85 KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Evan Marshall <evan@evergreen-ai.com>
Cc: support@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-20T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Livechat streaming delays starting ~09:00 PDT

Evan — thanks for the heads-up and the sample IDs. We're marking this as high priority. Initial notes:

1) I've escalated to SRE and the realtime team; on-call is investigating edge shards in us-west.
2) Immediate customer-side actions you can take (no code deploy):
   - Enable streaming fallback: set streaming_fallback=true in your client so the UI falls back to poll-style responses when a stream stalls.
   - Reduce max_stream_chunk_size to 512 bytes to force smaller, more frequent chunks (helps mask tail latency).
   - Add exponential retry with jitter on streaming handshake failures (1s, 2s, 4s).

3) Can you share 3 full request-ids (headers + body) and approximate timestamps for two affected conversations? That will speed correlation.

I'll send an internal note with diagnostic steps and come back with a quick playbook. Stand by for an update in ~30–60 minutes.

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Date: 2028-07-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Livechat streaming delays — Evergreen AI — initial triage

Quick triage summary and temporary mitigation tested (results below):

Root cause hypothesis (what we saw):
- At ~08:58–09:05 PDT a sustained GC latency event on a tokenizer preprocessor host caused the controller's batching window to grow from its normal ~10–15ms to ~120–140ms for a subset of streaming flows. That amplified tail latency for streaming-only connections (those depend on small, frequent writes).
- Simultaneously Evergreen ramped a small traffic spike after a feature flag flip which produced a burst of previously uncached prefixes — cache-miss rate spiked and increased per-request work.
- Combined effect: longer batch windows + cache work = 5–12s intermittent pauses for streaming chunk delivery. Polling/generation unaffected because those requests are handled by a different path with larger batch amortization.

What we did (short-term, validated):
1) Forced Evergreen routing to fallback model-variant (non-stream-optimized) for the tenant — streaming calls now fall back to poll-style responses for the affected sessions. Verified mean client-visible chunk pause dropped to <300ms.
2) Deployed a targeted controller patch to cap streaming batch-window to 25ms for tenants experiencing tail-latency >1s. This reduces tail spikes while we root cause the tokenizer GC issue.
3) Increased prefix cache replication for Evergreen's shard to lower cache-miss rate.

Customer-facing mitigations you can share with Evergreen (minimal risk):
- Toggle streaming_fallback=true (we can also flip server-side if they prefer).
- Reduce max_stream_chunk_size to 512 and increase client-side chunk-tolerance to handle more frequent writes.
- Implement client-side streaming handshake retry with exponential backoff.

Next steps (mid-term):
- SRE will patch tokenizer hosts to address GC and push a GC tuning profile; postmortem and permanent fix targeted in INF-4932.
- We'll schedule a maintenance window to shift Evergreen to a more resilient routing tier next week (tentative: 2028-07-22 02:00–04:00 UTC).

I've attached traces and a short remediation playbook you can share with the customer. I'll keep you updated as we verify root cause and close the ticket.

Marissa Cole
Principal Engineer, Realtime Services
marissa@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Evan Marshall <evan@evergreen-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Evergreen AI — mitigation summary and next steps (Live chat slowdown)

Evan — quick summary of what we did and what you can do now to reduce customer-visible impact. Full technical postmortem (INF-4932) will follow once SRE finishes analysis.

What we did for you (server-side, completed):
- Temporarily routed Evergreen streaming traffic to a fallback model-variant that returns poll-style frames for in-flight sessions. This is live and lowering perceived pauses.
- Deployed a controller cap to limit streaming batch-window to 25ms for tenants showing tail latency >1s.
- Scaled prefix cache replication for Evergreen's shards.

Actions we recommend you apply client-side immediately (if you can):
1) Set streaming_fallback=true (toggle on the client). This causes the client to gracefully switch to poll-mode when a stream stalls.
2) Reduce max_stream_chunk_size to 512 bytes. Example JSON: {
   "streaming_fallback": true,
   "max_stream_chunk_size": 512
}
3) Add exponential backoff on streaming handshake failures and retry the stream handshake up to 3 times before falling back to poll.

Short-term timeline:
- We will monitor Evergreen traffic over the next 48 hours. If tail latency remains controlled we will keep the routing change for 72 hours and then roll back once tokenizer hosts are patched.
- We propose a maintenance window on 2028-07-22 to apply the permanent GC tuning and a controller release. We'll confirm schedule and customer impact ahead of time.

Compensation: We're prepared to offer a service credit for the customer-facing impact window. I'll loop in your account rep to finalize.

Attachments: remediation-playbook-v1.pdf (client steps and server flags) and the traces we collected.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the playbook and any config changes.

Thanks for the quick report — and sorry for the disruption. Please reply with the three full request-ids and any additional traces if you can.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
